blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Double taxation is when the same income is taxed twice. One country taxes it because the money was earned there. Another country taxes it because the taxpayer lives there. Without rules, cross-border income would be punished twice — just for crossing a border.

To stop this, most countries sign double taxation treaties. The treaty says who can tax first. It also says how much relief the other country must give. So the total tax is usually close to the tax in a single country.

Double taxation relief is not exotic. It is a normal, practical part of doing business across borders. It is also an essential thing to check before any international deal is signed.

items.q: When does double taxation happen?
options: When a company pays no tax
When two people share one salary
When a country has very high taxes
When the same income is taxed twice
items.why: "Double taxation is when the same income is taxed twice."

items.q: Why do most countries sign double taxation treaties?
options: To close their borders to business
To stop the same income being taxed twice
To hide income from other countries
To raise taxes for both countries
items.why: "To stop this, most countries sign double taxation treaties."

items.q: What does the treaty decide?
options: How much salary a worker gets
When the deal must be signed
Who can tax first and how much relief to give
items.why: "The treaty says who can tax first… how much relief the other country must give."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which idea?
options: You should check the treaty before a deal.
Double taxation relief is rare and strange.
The same income can be taxed in two countries.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz "relief is not exotic" — ele discordaria de chamá-lo de raro e estranho.

items.q: The text suggests that, with a treaty, a cross-border business…
options: pays about the same as in a single country
items.why: Inferência: "the total tax is usually close to the tax in a single country" — o tratado evita o dobro.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James explicando um exemplo simples para um novo analista. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, let me show you with a simple example. It is easier than it sounds. Imagine our client earns a fee of ten thousand pounds. The work was done in Brazil, but the client lives in the UK. So both countries want to tax the same fee.

Brazil says: the money was earned here, so we tax it first. The UK says: the taxpayer lives here, so we can tax it too. Without a treaty, the same ten thousand pounds is taxed twice. That is double taxation, and it is not fair. The client would be punished just for working across a border.

But there is a treaty between the two countries. The treaty says Brazil taxes the fee first. Then the UK gives relief for the tax already paid in Brazil. So the client does not pay the full tax twice. The total tax is close to a normal, single-country deal.

This is why we always check the treaty before we sign. It is not exotic — it is a normal, everyday step. If you forget it, the client can lose real money for nothing. So put it on your list for every international deal.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is the fee in James's example?
items.why: "our client earns a fee of ten thousand pounds."

items.q: Where was the work done, and where does the client live?
options: Work in the UK; client lives in Brazil
Work in Brazil; client lives in the UK
items.why: "The work was done in Brazil, but the client lives in the UK."

items.q: According to the treaty, who taxes the fee first?
items.why: "The treaty says Brazil taxes the fee first."

items.q: Why does the UK give relief?
options: Because tax was already paid in Brazil
Because the UK has no taxes
Because the fee is too small to tax
items.why: Inferência: o alívio existe para evitar cobrar de novo o que já foi pago no Brasil.

items.q: What does James think you should always do before signing?
items.why: Inferência: "we always check the treaty before we sign… If you forget it, the client can lose money."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Every worker who pays tax is a taxpayer." A taxpayer is…
items.why: Taxpayer = contribuinte, quem paga o imposto.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The two countries signed a ___ to stop double taxation."
items.why: Treaty = tratado, o acordo entre os países.

items.q: "The UK gives relief for tax already paid abroad." Relief here means…
options: a reduction in the tax you must pay
items.why: Relief = alívio / abatimento no imposto.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "This ___ deal involves a client in Brazil and a client in the UK."
items.why: Cross-border = transfronteiriço, que atravessa a fronteira entre países.

items.q: "You must always earn money before you can save it." To earn means to…
items.why: To earn = ganhar (dinheiro pelo trabalho).

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de negócios. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager still has to sign off on the deal." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We will roll out the new rule country by country." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = colocar em prática aos poucos.

items.q: "Let's go over the treaty before the meeting." To go over means to…
items.why: Go over = revisar, checar com cuidado.

items.q: "The team agreed on the plan but never followed through." They…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Please look into the tax rules for this deal." To look into means to…
items.why: Look into = investigar, estudar um assunto.
